title: How to write a baseline before a workflow goes live
description: Pick the request type, agree one main measure and what counts as resolved, then record how your team handles those requests today over a typical period.

summary.question: How do I write a baseline before a workflow goes live?
summary.answer: Pick the request type, agree one main measure and what counts as resolved, then record how your team handles those requests today over a typical period. Write it down before go-live and compare with it, measured the same way, at every review.
takeaways: Write the baseline before anything goes live; it cannot be rebuilt honestly afterwards.
Agree what counts as resolved before you start measuring.
Use one main measure, such as staff minutes per resolved request.
Record exceptions and unresolved requests separately, not as resolved.
Measure the current process and the new workflow the same way.

scope.covers: What a baseline is, what to record in it, how long to measure, and how to use it at each review.
scope.excludes: Statistical methods, settings for a specific software product, and price or savings figures.
scope.instead: How to count staff time for each resolved request is covered in the guide to staff minutes per resolved request.

sections.heading: What is a baseline?
paragraphs: A baseline is a written record of how your team handles a type of request today. It is the starting point that every later result is compared with, so you can see whether a live workflow is actually better than the way you worked before.
Without one, a review can only say what happened after go-live, not whether it improved anything.

sections.heading: What should a baseline record?
paragraphs: Keep it short enough that the same person can measure it again later in exactly the same way.
list: The type of request it covers, for example vehicle enquiries at one dealership or service-visit requests at one service desk.
What counts as resolved: the person responsible confirms the outcome, such as a test drive confirmed by staff.
The main measure, for example staff minutes per resolved request, counting review, corrections and follow-up time.
How many requests were resolved, handed off, still open or abandoned during the period.
The exceptions: requests that did not fit the normal process, and who handled them.
The period measured and how the numbers were collected.

links.label: What is staff minutes per resolved request?

sections.heading: How do you collect the numbers?
paragraphs: Measure the current process over a typical period, before the new workflow goes live. A simple log or a timed sample of typical requests is enough, as long as you measure the current process and the new workflow the same way.
Requests that were only handed off, are still open or were abandoned do not count as resolved. Track them separately so the baseline is not flattered.

sections.heading: Which measure should a dealership use?
paragraphs: Choose the measure that matches the outcome the team cares about. For dealership sales and service enquiries, the suggested measure is enquiries with a confirmed next step.
list: Count enquiries with a confirmed next step, such as a booked test drive or a confirmed service visit.
Track response time, attended appointments, unresolved leads and the staff effort required.

sections.heading: How do you use the baseline once the workflow is live?
paragraphs: Compare with the baseline at every review, using the same definition of resolved and the same way of counting. Read the exceptions next to the main measure: a rising exception count can explain a result, and it shows which rules need to change.

sections.heading: How does CarSalesTeam use a baseline?
paragraphs: We record your current process before going live, then track the outcome, the exceptions and the staff time needed to get there. The workflows, approval rules, fees, limits and how results are measured are agreed first, and the rules are tested on sample data before anything goes live.

faq.a: A written record of how your team handles a type of request today, used to compare results once a new workflow is live.

faq.q: When should the baseline be written?
faq.a: Before the workflow goes live, over a typical period of normal work.

faq.q: Do I need special software to measure a baseline?
faq.a: No. A simple log or a timed sample of typical requests is enough, as long as you measure the new workflow the same way.

faq.q: Do handed-off requests count as resolved?
faq.a: No. Only requests the person responsible confirms as done count. Track the rest separately.
